description: Captures files from a directory tree on an SFTP server, parsing each file (CSV/JSON/Avro/protobuf/W3C log, optionally compressed) into records.

scheme.description: ssh.PublicKeys with a signer parsed from the PEM private key in credentials.sshKey; username from credentials.username. Passphrase-protected keys are not supported (plain ParsePrivateKey, no passphrase field).

credentialModes.name: Legacy top-level username/password (undocumented, hidden from the config schema)

artifacts: an SSH connection and SFTP subsystem session for the lifetime of the process
continuity.notes: Nothing is left on the customer's SFTP server: the connector only reads (ReadDir/Stat/Open). Pausing between sweeps costs nothing as long as the customer does not delete files before we list them; the mtime cursor (state.minBound) is held entirely on our side, so an arbitrarily long pause is safe. Risk is on our side only in the sense that files deleted from the server while we are paused are never captured, and files whose mtime is rewound below minBound while we are paused are silently skipped forever.

configFields.name: address
configFields.description: Host and port of the SFTP server, e.g. myserver.com:22. Passed verbatim to ssh.Dial("tcp", ...); there is no default port, the port must be included.

configFields.name: credentials.sshKey
configFields.description: Multiline PEM private key; required when credentials.type is "sshKey".

configFields.name: username
configFields.description: Legacy top-level field, hidden from the generated schema (jsonschema:"-") but still accepted and used as a fallback when credentials.username is empty.

configFields.name: password
configFields.description: Legacy top-level field, hidden from the generated schema and NOT marked secret; used when credentials.type is empty.

configFields.name: directory
configFields.description: Absolute, path.Clean-normalized root directory. All files in it and its subdirectories are captured. Validated at connect time via Stat, falling back to RealPath+ReadDir for servers (e.g. AWS Transfer Family) that reject Stat.

configFields.name: matchFiles
configFields.description: Go RE2 regex; compiled at Validate time. Documented as matching the path relative to the directory, but applied to the full listed path (see unionMisfits).

configFields.name: advanced.ascendingKeys
configFields.description: Declares that files are written in ascending lexicographic order so lexical path ordering matches mtime ordering. Switches the framework into monotonic mode: minBound is never advanced and the next sweep resumes the listing from the last processed path instead of re-walking from the root.

configFields.name: parser.format
configFields.description: One of auto (default), csv, json, avro, protobuf, w3cExtendedLog. CSV carries its own sub-config (delimiter, encoding, escape, quote, lineEnding, headers, errorThreshold).

configFields.name: parser.compression
configFields.description: One of gzip, zip, zstd, none, or null = Auto (sniffed).

configFields.name: stream
configFields.description: Absolute path prefix to sweep. Discovery proposes a single binding whose stream is the configured directory.

discovery.method: Single synthetic binding rooted at the configured directory (no server-side enumeration at discover time); the actual file set is enumerated per sweep by a recursive SFTP ReadDir walk.
discovery.querySketch: Discover -> one binding { stream: config.directory }, recommendedName = directory with leading/trailing '/' trimmed (or "root"), key = [/_meta/file, /_meta/offset], document schema is a minimal x-infer-schema object.
excludes: zero-byte objects (treated as directory placeholders, always skipped)
symlinks that resolve to directories (logged and skipped; never descended)
subdirectory entries themselves (recursive listings emit only files)
paths outside this shard's key range (hardware-hash of the path)

schedule.description: Pull performs exactly one sweep per binding and then returns; there is no in-connector sleep or interval. Re-sweep cadence is decided by the Flow runtime restarting the connector, which is outside this repo.

incremental.listing: Recursive, lexically-ordered, lazy depth-first walk driven by an explicit stack. newSftpListing seeds the stack with ReadDir(prefix); each pushDir reads one directory, drops entries whose full path sorts below StartAt, sorts the remainder in REVERSE lexical order and appends, so Next() pops in ascending lexical order. Directory entries are pushed (descended) rather than emitted; symlinks are Stat'd and, if they resolve to directories, skipped entirely. Resume across sweeps is by path: the framework passes Query.StartAt = state.path (the last file whose parse completed), so a crashed or restarted sweep re-walks the tree but re-lists only from that path onward. Within a single file, resume is by record count: state.records survives the checkpoint and the file is re-opened from byte 0 and re-parsed with the first N records suppressed.

authTierRationale: Both offered modes are a single self-serve secret the user already has for their own SFTP server: a password, or a PEM private key pasted into a multiline field. No OAuth app registration and no refresh token anywhere in the connector (Source.Oauth2 is left nil). Note the SSH key mode has no passphrase field, so users must supply an unencrypted key -- still T1 in effort, but it forces them to hold a passphrase-less key.

unionMisfits.description: The `objects` PullSpec has no field for the incremental cursor, which for this connector is the whole story. The cursor is an mtime WINDOW held in connector state, not a field on a record: state.minBound (exclusive lower) .. state.maxBound (exclusive upper), where maxBound is sampled once per sweep as round(now - 30s) and minBound advances after each completed sweep to maxMod (the largest mtime actually processed), NOT to maxBound. Listing order (lexical path) and cursor (mtime) are two different axes, and `objects` can express only the former.

cursor.monotonicModeOverride: when advanced.ascendingKeys is set, minBound is never advanced and resume is purely by lexical path

unionMisfits.description: Null is correct in that no byte-range request is issued, but the read is not a naive whole-object GET either: sftp.File.WriteTo runs concurrent buffered reads into an io.Pipe. And intra-file resume DOES exist -- it is expressed in records, not bytes (skip the first N parsed records after re-reading the file from the start).

proposedShape.readConcurrency: sftp WriteTo concurrent buffered reads via io.Pipe

unionMisfits.description: There is no slot for transport-security posture. Host-key verification is disabled unconditionally (ssh.InsecureIgnoreHostKey) and two weak key-exchange algorithms are added to the defaults, including diffie-hellman-group1-sha1. That is a property of the connection, not of any one credential mode, and a consumer of this JSON has nowhere to see it.

matchFiles is documented as matching the path relative to the configured directory, but the framework applies the compiled regex to the full listed path (which for this connector is the absolute server path). A user writing an anchored regex such as `^data/.*\.csv$` matches nothing. There is no field to record a doc/behaviour divergence.

abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: The connector performs exactly one sweep per Pull invocation and returns; no interval, cron, or sleep exists anywhere in source-sftp or filesource. The re-invocation cadence lives in the Flow runtime, which is not in this repository.
abstained.streams[0].cursorField: There is no per-record cursor field. Incrementality is driven by file modification time held in connector state (minBound/maxBound), which is not a document field, and the emitted documents carry only /_meta/file and /_meta/offset plus whatever the parser infers.
abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultPort: objectStore transports have no port field in the schema, and the connector defines no default: `address` is passed verbatim to ssh.Dial and the user must include ':22' themselves. A missing port produces a dial error, not a default.
abstained.streams[0].writeDisposition: Chose "merge" because the collection key is (file, offset), so re-capturing a modified file overwrites the same keys rather than duplicating. But the connector itself never expresses a disposition -- that is Flow collection reduction semantics, and deletion of a source file produces no tombstone.
abstained.streams[0].supportedSyncModes: The resource schema carries a syncMode field but it is hidden (jsonschema:"-") and never read; the sweep is always the same mtime-windowed incremental walk. A true full refresh is only achievable by resetting connector state.
